transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands
Date: 2026-04-22 10:00 PDT | Duration: 68 minutes | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (CEO), Diego Alvarez (CTO), Priya Nair (VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Head of Product), Zoe Park (Head of Sales), Arjun Rao (Head of Research), Hannah Lee (Head of CS), + ~150 employees

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick note we started a bit late, so we'll try to keep to the 60-70 minute window and leave time for questions. Big updates this month, lots to be proud of.

[00:00:15] Diego Alvarez: I'll kick off with the reliability and infra update. Over the last quarter our P95 latency across hosted endpoints improved by about 12% after shipping the new KV-cache routing. There was one incident on April 6 where a memthreshold bug caused queueing on a Dedicated pool, we traced it to a kernel fallback on older drivers - Hannah, you can add the rest in the incident review later.

[00:00:45] Hannah Lee: Yeah, incident postmortem is in the IT channel, but tl;dr: customer impact was limited to two Dedicated tenants, we invoked fallback to compatible quantized variants and the rollback took ~22 minutes. We're rolling out driver compatibility tests in our CI.

[00:01:20] Priya Nair: On the engineering roadmap, Q2 is about stabilization and cost/perf wins. The batcher rewrite is in staging and initial tests show 18-25% token-cost reduction for chat workloads. There's work to do on the autoscaler behavior for heterogeneous GPUs - we need more real-world traces to tune policies.

[00:01:55] Liam O'Connor: Product highlights - shipping streaming function-calls to GA by end of May, plus structured output templates for retrieval-augmented apps. Also we plan a feature flag for model pinning per-route, which should help customers with strict compliance rollouts.

[00:02:20] Zoe Park: Sales update - we closed two mid-market Dedicated deals this month and are in late-stage talks with a large financial services POC for Private (VPC + on-prem). Their compliance asks are heavy: FIPS, HSM integration, and data residency. We are coordinating with security to put together the pack.

[00:02:45] Maya Chen: Great - this aligns with our thesis that people want predictable serving. Arjun, quick note on research and model onboarding.

[00:02:52] Arjun Rao: We're streamlining model variance testing - automated quality/regression checks for new quantizations. We found a small regression on conversational safety for one 4-bit recipe; it's subtle but the evals flagged it, so we reverted that recipe for public models.

[00:03:15] Speaker 1: (inaudible) question about the policy for rolling back across Dedicated tenants - is that automatic or manual?

[00:03:23] Priya Nair: It's a hybrid; safe rollbacks need human signoff for cross-tenant changes, but we can auto-fallback to compatible model variants on a per-request basis. We're working on clearer runbooks.

[00:03:40] Maya Chen: Quick hiring note - we're at ~150 headcount, hiring for SRE, infra software, and two product managers. We want to accelerate SRE hiring given the incident profile.

[00:04:00] Diego Alvarez: Ops update: new tracing hooks in the console give token-level breakdowns per model route. Early feedback from a few customers in pilot was that it made cost attribution much easier - helps them decide between batching and lower-precision models.

[00:04:30] Zoe Park: On pricing and packaging, customers keep asking about cost transparency with Dedicated vs Hosted. We plan to publish a benchmarking playbook - this will include sample configuration, expected latency/cost tradeoffs, and when to choose Private. Liam will lead the doc.

[00:04:55] Liam O'Connor: Yep, working on the playbook. Also, to be realistic, there are still workloads where we recommend Dedicated or Private because they need VPC connectivity or HSM integration. We'll provide concrete examples.

[00:05:15] Audience question (chat): Can you share more detail on the BankPilot POC?

[00:05:20] Zoe Park: BankPilot is a financial services POC; they wanted private deployment, strict audit logs and HSM for keys. We ran a two-week benchmark, they were impressed with latency but asked for SOC2 evidence and detailed audit capabilities. We're close to contracting - will share the case study.

[00:05:45] Arjun Rao: Small demo note - our research infra now supports kernel selection for Llama-like architectures in staging; early perf gains are promising but we still need more representative load tests.

[00:06:10] Priya Nair: On the cost/performance initiative: the engineering org will run a two-sprint blitz to optimize default batching, KV cache TTL defaults, and quantization recipes. Goal is ~20% effective unit-cost reduction for typical chat workloads without materially impacting P95 latency.

[00:06:40] Maya Chen: OK, let's talk goals and metrics for the quarter. Revenue targets are motioned in the all-hands deck - we've got solid pipeline for Dedicated bookings. Our operational focus is to reduce mean time to mitigation for infra incidents to under 15 minutes.

[00:07:05] Hannah Lee: We also need to tighten our runbook handoffs between SE and SRE during customer escalations; action item for CS and Eng to co-author.

[00:07:25] Speaker 2: Quick clarification - are we deprecating any older model variants?

[00:07:30] Arjun Rao: Not broadly, but we will mark a few older quant recipes as legacy and stop recommending them. We'll still support but won't optimize.

[00:07:45] Maya Chen: Finance and legal note - pricing tiers for Reserved Dedicated capacity are being finalized; contract templates for Private will include clearer SLAs and security appendices. Legal to share with sales this week.

[00:08:05] Zoe Park: On churn: a couple of smaller customers churned due to cost concerns; we are following up to see if a different config (more caching, different batching) would've helped. We should be proactive and provide optimization playbooks.

[00:08:30] Audience question (Q&A): How do we prioritize feature requests versus platform reliability?

[00:08:40] Maya Chen: Short answer: reliability first for mission-critical infra; product features that directly improve customer's ability to ship (like streaming function-calls) are second. We'll keep balancing - execs will review triage weekly.

[00:09:05] Diego Alvarez: Also, a quick thing on telemetry: we're adding per-route error budgets to the console so teams can see when a route is trending towards its SLO and get automated alerts.

[00:09:30] Liam O'Connor: Roadmap milestone: GA for streaming function-calls (end of May), model pinning by June, and an improved console experience for cost attribution by mid-July.

[00:09:50] Maya Chen: Open floor for a short AMA - please drop questions in chat.

[00:10:00] Question (from engineering): What's the plan for multi-region routing to reduce latency for APAC?

[00:10:10] Priya Nair: We're expanding Dedicated pools in APAC region partners this quarter; initially a soft-launch in Singapore region, more to come. We will also add smart routing policies for region preference.

[00:10:30] Question (from sales): For large private deals, what's the expected ramp time for on-prem installs?

[00:10:36] Hannah Lee: Typical on-prem + Private control-plane installs are 6-10 weeks depending on network and compliance work. If the customer requires air-gapped installs, add 4-6 weeks for packaging and validation.

[00:11:05] Audience laughter / brief cross-talk.

[00:11:20] Diego Alvarez: One thing I want to flag: kernel compatibility across vendor drivers remains a risk. We're investing in more robust fallbacks and a driver test matrix in CI.

[00:11:45] Maya Chen: Alright, wrapping up - thanks to everyone. Recap of asks: product to share playbook, eng to run cost/perf blitz, security to package Private docs, and hiring to prioritize SRE.

[00:12:10] Maya Chen: Last note - big kudos to the team shipping Dedicated autoscaler improvements; that was a tough one. We'll celebrate in next week's retro.

[00:12:25] End of formal presentation - open networking for teams for the next 50 minutes (recording continues but fewer formal remarks).

[00:13:00] (Informal chattiness; small team updates)

[00:28:15] Speaker 3: Quick plug - town hall for research on Wednesday, 9am PT.

[00:35:40] Speaker 4: Reminder: office hours for benchmarking are available - sign up via the internal calendar.

[00:50:05] Maya Chen: Closing remarks - remember to file action items and reach out to your managers if you have questions. Thanks, everyone.

[00:52:00] Recording ends (informal chatter continues for a few minutes).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings in the informal section, proper nouns sometimes transcribed inconsistently (e.g., BankPilot heard as BankPilot, Bank Pilot). Some timestamps approximate when recording was resumed after formal part.
